name: Islo

modes.label: Pay-as-you-go (Team list rates)
modes.note: CPU billed per allocated core while running; RAM per provisioned GB; custom integer vcpus/memory_mb/disk_gb with no published limits. Idle-but-running bills at full rate until pause_after_idle fires. Paused/stopped: $0 compute. Basis verified 2026-09-28: CPU "$0.07/CPU-hour" billed "per core while the env runs"; memory "per GB you provision" (https://islo.dev/pricing). pause_after_idle: "Pause after this many seconds without activity (no exec, file I/O, port traffic, etc.)" (https://docs.islo.dev/concepts/sandbox-lifecycle.md).

evidence.quote: Gateways control how your sandbox connects to external services. A gateway profile is a network policy plus an ordered set of rules
if nothing matches, the profile's `--default-action` decides

plans.name: Free
plans.note: Signup credits, no card; amount unpublished. 5-concurrent cap per launch press coverage (The New Stack), not on islo.dev.

plans.name: Team
plans.note: Pay-as-you-go at list rates; no seat licenses. 50 concurrent running sandboxes per press coverage; paused sandboxes don't count.

plans.name: AWS Marketplace Team Starter
plans.note: $50/month contract = $50 monthly credits ('294 hours compute for most customers'), no refunds; overage handling and rollover unspecified in listing. Concurrency 50 assumed = Team plan ('Team Starter Package'); was null, which let the engine bypass the Team 50-concurrent cap via this plan (verifier 2026-09-28).

plans.name: Enterprise / BYOC
plans.note: Custom packages; FAQ: 'You still pay for compute time. BYOC deployment terms may vary.'

perf_source: No benchmark row: provider is not in ComputeSDK results or the HPC run (as of 2026-09-28). See research/perf-map.json.

knobs.label: Idle tail before pause_after_idle (x session hours)
knobs.why: Idle-but-running sandboxes bill full allocated CPU/RAM until the pause_after_idle lifecycle timer fires; without a policy they bill until deleted, and the policy is immutable after creation. Paused = $0 compute. Factor = (session + idle timer) / session.

caveats: Billing granularity and minimum per start unpublished ('billed per hour' / 'per vCPU-hour'); per-second metering not confirmed.
Whether disk is billed while paused/stopped is unresolved: FAQ says 'No charge when stopped' but storage is a listed $0.0007/GB-h meter.
Named snapshot storage price unpublished (snapshot_gib_month null); if billed at the disk rate it would be $0.511/GB-month.
Disk billed per provisioned GB with no stated free allowance; included_disk_gib=0 reflects that, and the engine should add W.disk x $0.0007/GB-h while running.
Free (5 concurrent) / Team (50 concurrent) / Enterprise tiers come from launch press coverage (The New Stack, May 2026), not an Islo page.
Signup credit amount unpublished; Harbor users get $250 one-time via promo code HARBOR250 (not modeled in free.one_time_credit).
Egress, IPv4 and region pricing unpublished; no public IPv4 product (HTTPS shares + CLI tunnel only).
Gateway inference (Islo-managed LLMs) draws from the same credits at unpublished token rates.
Lifecycle policy (pause_after_idle etc.) is immutable after creation; sandboxes without it bill at full rate while idle.
Heavy paused sandboxes can take 5-7 min to become resumable (third-party report).
No benchmark data for islo in benchmarks.json.

Official RL page cost example bills 10-minute tasks pro rata (500 tasks x ~10 min at 4 vCPU / 1 GB / ~2 GB disk = $26.78, ~$0.054/task), so metering is at least sub-hour in practice. Exact granularity and per-start minimum are still unpublished; the engine should not assume hourly rounding.

Official pages show 300 concurrent Harbor rollouts ('--n-concurrent 300', 'hundreds of concurrent rollouts'), well above the press-reported 50-concurrent Team cap. The cap is probably raisable, but it is still not published on any Islo page.

fleet.verification: Official pricing says signup credits with no card; further screening not published.
fleet.tiers: Launch coverage reports Free 5, Team 50, Enterprise custom; current official pricing does not republish numeric tier limits.
fleet.notes: Third-party-reported concurrency: The New Stack launch article, not independently confirmed by current official quota docs. Thus 10/50 via reported Team path only; 300/1,000 custom unverified. Lifecycle docs confirm paused sandboxes do not count toward running quota. Launch article also mentions private beta; confirm current admission. Current self-serve tier activation/increase mechanism is not independently verified, so raise remains null.

snapshot_auto.quote: When a timer fires, the platform **pauses** the VM: state is snapshotted, compute is released, and the sandbox no longer counts against running-sandbox quotas. Paused sandboxes keep their filesystem and can be resumed.
snapshot_auto.note: Opt-in lifecycle policy set at creation (immutable): pause_after_idle (no exec/file I/O/port traffic) and/or pause_after (active-runtime cap); auto_resume=on_activity resumes transparently on the next exec/file/webhook. Memory included: 'files, processes, and in-memory state are restored on resume' (https://docs.islo.dev/cli/sandbox-commands.md, islo pause). Without a policy nothing pauses automatically.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: Snapshots let you capture the complete state of a running sandbox and restore it later.
snapshot_on_demand.note: Named snapshots (islo snapshot save / POST snapshots) are filesystem-only ('The snapshot captures the entire filesystem state'), from a running sandbox; restore always creates a NEW sandbox ('Restoring from a snapshot creates a new sandbox'), so they work as templates/forks (many sandboxes from one snapshot). Memory-including state is only via pause/resume of the same sandbox (manual islo pause or API).

harness_api.quote: Harness and model live on the `run_agent` step, never in `line.toml`.
harness_api.note: Jobs / factory lines (API + CLI) run a first-party run_agent step with harness codex, claude, cursor or opencode (+ 'custom' exec) and a prompt; runs expose events (islo factory line-run events), follow-ups and mid-stage agent turns (line-run follow-up / agent-turn / ask), steer/stop/retry. Harness list from Islo's own skills repo (harness-models-knowledge.md: '`harness` must be a literal (`codex`, `claude`, `cursor`, or `opencode`)'). Also CLI: 'islo use --agent claude --task "..."' starts Claude Code/Cursor/Codex in a persistent background session and resumes Claude Code sessions on reconnect (https://docs.islo.dev/cli/agent-integration.md).

egress_allowlist.quote: A gateway profile is a network policy plus an ordered set of rules — each rule matches outbound traffic by host (and optionally path/method) and decides whether to allow it, deny it, or inject credentials before forwarding.
egress_allowlist.note: Gateway profile per sandbox: --default-action allow|deny (default-deny possible), host globs ('*.anthropic.com'), --internet-access true/false (also internet_enabled on create-sandbox). Host-based; no IP/CIDR rules documented. Rules changed after creation need sandbox recreate/reconnect.

egress_http_rules.quote: Restrict to one or more HTTP methods (`GET`, `POST`, …)
egress_http_rules.note: Per-rule path pattern, HTTP methods, rate limit (rpm), and request/response content filters (regex, content-type, size-limit, and an LLM 'judge' filter with Anthropic/OpenAI model per the API reference create-gateway-rule).

ingress_rules.quote: Islo lets you create shareable URLs for HTTP services running inside your sandbox.
ingress_rules.note: Ports are not public by default: you choose a port to share (islo share <sandbox> [port]) with a TTL (default 24h, e.g. 30m-7d) and revoke with islo unshare; shares are public HTTPS URLs (API: 'Create a temporary public share for a sandbox port'), no auth/IP allowlist on the share itself. Non-HTTP access via authenticated islo port-forward tunnel. Incoming webhooks authenticate (HMAC/bearer/basic) before delivering to a port.

guest_firewall.note: Each sandbox is 'a microVM with its own kernel' (https://islo.dev/sandboxes) with root/sudo (setup scripts use sudo apt-get; Docker inside supported), so iptables/nftables inside should work. Not documented.

secret_proxy.quote: Credentials never reach the sandbox process — authentication happens at the host/network layer.
secret_proxy.note: Gateway rules inject a stored provider key as bearer/basic/custom header for any host; integrations cover GitHub, Slack, Anthropic/OpenAI/Cursor and tenant custom services (API key or OAuth). Sandboxes see phantom placeholder env vars (values starting 'islo_p') replaced on egress (islo-labs/skills gateway-integrations.md). AWS: IAM role assumed via STS through the gateway, no long-lived keys in the sandbox (https://docs.islo.dev/integrations/aws.md). Git over HTTPS to GitHub covered; SSH/database protocols not documented. Islo inference (gateway.islo.dev) additionally provides platform-owned model credentials.

volume_attach.note: Create-sandbox schema has disk_gb but no volume/mount fields; no volume concept anywhere in the docs index. Persistence is via pause/resume and snapshots. Users can self-mount S3 with mount-s3 via the AWS cloud-role integration (third-party FUSE, not a first-party volume).

volume_shared.note: No shared volume/filesystem product. Sharing between sandboxes is only via snapshots (copy) or a user-mounted S3 bucket (mount-s3 over the AWS integration, read-write per IAM policy). 'Knowledge' is a versioned document store API, not a filesystem.

nested_virt.quote: ISOLATION microVM per agent computer. Stronger boundary than containers alone for untrusted or production-adjacent work.
nested_virt.note: Not documented either way. Derived: each sandbox is itself a microVM (Firecracker/cloud-hypervisor-style guest); such guests typically do not expose /dev/kvm for nested virtualization, and no docs mention nested virt, running VMs/emulators, or /dev/kvm inside a sandbox.

anti_bot.quote: An agent sandbox is an isolated computer where a coding agent runs shell commands, opens a browser, starts services, and calls APIs under policy constraints.
anti_bot.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Islo is infrastructure for coding agents (shell/services/APIs plus a generic browser for testing); no stealth/fingerprinting-evasion feature against bot detection is documented anywhere in the docs, marketing, or gateway pages.

captcha_solving.quote: An agent sandbox is an isolated computer where a coding agent runs shell commands, opens a browser, starts services, and calls APIs under policy constraints.
captcha_solving.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. No CAPTCHA-solving feature is mentioned anywhere in Islo's docs, product, or gateway pages; the product is coding-agent sandbox infrastructure, not a web-scraping/anti-bot service.

egress_ip_type.quote: Routes traffic — proxies through Islo's gateway so requests can be audited and rate-limited.
egress_ip_type.note: Islo runs cloud VMs (also sold via AWS Marketplace) with outbound traffic optionally routed through Islo's own gateway/proxy. No residential or mobile IP option is documented anywhere; egress is standard cloud/datacenter IP space. Not explicitly labeled 'datacenter' on any page.

fork_running.quote: Snapshots let you capture the complete state of a running sandbox and restore it later... Save a snapshot of a running sandbox: `islo snapshot save my-sandbox`... Create a new sandbox from a snapshot using `--snapshot`: `islo use new-sandbox --snapshot before-refactor`
fork_running.note: Snapshot save operates on a running sandbox without stopping/pausing it, and restoring the snapshot creates a brand-new sandbox (clone). The original keeps running throughout, so this satisfies cloning a running machine without stopping it (filesystem-only clone, not memory/processes).

live_resize.note: vCPU/memory/disk are set only in the create-sandbox request; no update/resize endpoint or CLI command for changing resources on a running sandbox is documented in the API reference or CLI sandbox-commands page. Resizing appears to require creating a new sandbox (e.g. from a snapshot) with different resources.

own_agent_api.quote: Which harnesses and models are supported? Islo is harness-agnostic. Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor run natively, and custom harnesses run on the same infrastructure.
own_agent_api.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Islo's API/CLI drives YOUR coding harness (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, custom) inside its sandboxes (harness_api) — it does not ship its own first-party task/browser/computer-use agent product to drive.

lang_python.quote: Setup scripts prepare a sandbox after sources are cloned but before you start using it — installing language runtimes, syncing dependencies, building tools. ... `islo add python 3.12` # Add the Python recipe pinned to 3.12
lang_python.note: Language runtimes are explicitly something you add via setup scripts/recipes (`islo add python <version>`), not something the docs describe as preinstalled in the default `islo-runner` image. No page states Python ships out of the box.

lang_node.quote: `islo add node 20` # Add the Node recipe pinned to 20
lang_node.note: Same as lang_python: Node.js is added via a setup-script recipe rather than documented as preinstalled by default in the base sandbox image.

public_ipv4.quote: Islo lets you create shareable URLs for HTTP services running inside your sandbox.
public_ipv4.note: No public IPv4 product is documented or priced anywhere (pricing page only lists CPU/memory/storage). Reaching a sandbox is via HTTPS share URLs, `islo port-forward` (local tunnel), or `islo ssh` (proxied SSH via `<name>.islo`) — not a dedicated public IPv4 address.

max_session_h.quote: How long can a computer stay up? Long enough for jobs measured in hours rather than seconds. Sessions survive disconnects and restarts, which is what makes unattended work possible.
max_session_h.note: No published hard ceiling on session length. Lifecycle policy fields (`pause_after`, `delete_after`) are optional and user-set at creation (https://docs.islo.dev/concepts/sandbox-lifecycle.md); without them a running sandbox is not automatically stopped, behaving like a VM that runs until you stop it.

persistent_disk.quote: When a timer fires, the platform **pauses** the VM: state is snapshotted, compute is released, and the sandbox no longer counts against running-sandbox quotas. Paused sandboxes keep their filesystem and can be resumed.
persistent_disk.note: Contradiction confirmed: card already lists pause_resume:true and snapshot:mem, and lifecycle docs state paused sandboxes 'keep their filesystem'. islo pause / API pause-sandbox (manual or via pause_after_idle/pause_after policy) preserves the full disk+memory state until islo resume. Default is no lifecycle policy set (manual pause/resume only) - there's no auto-delete-on-stop default; disk persists across pause/resume in all cases. Correcting persistent_disk to true.

memory_snapshot_fork.quote: The snapshot captures the entire filesystem state ... Restoring from a snapshot creates a new sandbox
memory_snapshot_fork.note: Named/on-demand snapshots (islo snapshot save, POST /snapshots) are explicitly filesystem-only, not memory - the card's own feature_evidence for snapshot_on_demand confirms this ('Snapshots... are filesystem-only'). The only memory-inclusive state capture is pause/resume of the SAME sandbox (no new sandbox id, no fork). No documented way to fork a running sandbox's live memory state into a new, independent sandbox. Confirms false.

desktop.quote: Islo gives you persistent, hardware-isolated sandbox environments that stay running... dedicated microVM
desktop.note: Full docs index (llms.txt) and CLI/API reference cover only exec, files, ports, sessions, SSH, sharing, gateways, snapshots and factory automations - no GUI/VNC/remote-desktop product anywhere. Islo sandboxes are headless Linux microVMs for code/CLI/agent work; no desktop environment is offered. Outside scope of the product.

computer_use.quote: Sandbox Commands: Islo CLI commands for creating, managing, and executing code in secure sandbox environments.
computer_use.note: No screenshot/mouse/keyboard-control API or computer-use tool documented anywhere in the docs index, CLI reference, or API reference (checked sandbox-commands.md, create-sandbox.md, agent-integration.md). Product surface is exec/files/ports only. Confirms false.

volumes.quote: disk_gb (integer, optional) ... memory_mb (integer, optional) ... vcpus (integer, optional)
volumes.note: Create-sandbox schema has only a per-sandbox disk_gb; no volume/mount/attach field anywhere in the API. This matches the card's own feature_evidence for volume_attach/volume_shared (both false: 'no volume concept anywhere in the docs index'; persistence is via pause/resume and snapshots, plus a third-party S3 FUSE mount). Confirms false.

mcp_server.quote: These docs are also available as an MCP server at https://docs.islo.dev/_mcp/server — point your AI agent at it to query Islo docs without leaving the editor.
mcp_server.note: The only MCP server Islo publishes is a documentation-search server for querying the docs themselves; there is no first-party MCP server exposing sandbox create/exec/file operations as MCP tools (agent integration is via SDK/CLI/API and islo-labs/skills, not MCP). Confirms false as a sandbox-control MCP server.

gpu.quote: Sandbox Lifecycle... Setup Scripts... Gateway Inference... Harbor... CLI Overview... Sandbox Commands...
gpu.note: GPU is never mentioned in the full documentation index, create-sandbox schema (vcpus/memory_mb/disk_gb only, no gpu field), CLI reference, or changelog. Card's own mode entry already has gpu:{} (empty) and gpu_types:[]. Confirms false.

windows.quote: Isolation | Shared kernel | Hardware-level ✓ - dedicated microVM
windows.note: Sandboxes are Linux microVMs (images are OCI/Docker images, e.g. ghcr.io/islo-labs/islo-runner:latest); the CLI installer supports macOS/Linux as the *client* machine only, not as a sandbox guest OS. No Windows sandbox guest offered anywhere in docs. Outside scope of a Linux-only microVM sandbox.

macos.quote: Install Islo CLI on macOS or Linux using the one-liner script.
macos.note: macOS/Linux support refers to the local CLI client, not the sandbox guest OS - sandboxes run as Linux microVMs from OCI images. No macOS guest sandbox is offered. Outside scope of a Linux-only microVM sandbox product.

self_host.note: All sandbox/compute operations go through Islo-operated regional endpoints (ca.compute.islo.dev, api.islo.dev); the only enterprise custom option documented is BYOC (bring-your-own-cloud, still Islo-managed/billed per the card's Enterprise plan note: 'You still pay for compute time'), not a self-hosted/on-prem deployment of the full Islo control plane. No self-hosting docs found. Confirms false.

open_source.quote: background-agents: An open-source background agents coding system (fork); skills: islo.dev skills; langchain-islo: Islo (islo.dev) sandbox integration for Deep Agents
open_source.note: islo-labs' public GitHub repos are SDK integrations, skills, and example/tooling projects (langchain-islo, claude-managed-agents, skills, recipes, reward-hack-bench) - none of them is the core sandbox/VM platform (compute engine, control plane, hypervisor). The platform itself (api.islo.dev / ca.compute.islo.dev) is closed-source SaaS. Confirms false.

eu_data_residency.note: The regions API's own example response lists only a US West region, matching the card's regions:["us"]. No EU region key or EU data-residency claim found on any Islo page. Confirms false.

static_egress_ip.quote: Applies network policies — controls which external endpoints the sandbox can reach... Routes traffic — proxies through Islo's gateway so requests can be audited and rate-limited.
static_egress_ip.note: Egress is host/path-rule based through Islo's shared gateway proxy; no page (gateway docs, gateway/security marketing pages, AWS integration) mentions a fixed/static outbound IP address a customer could allowlist. Absence across all egress-control docs indicates the feature isn't offered.

arm64.note: That table is architecture support for the local Islo CLI client (macOS/Linux, incl. Apple Silicon), not the sandbox guest. The sandbox create API (vcpus/memory_mb/disk_gb only, no architecture field) and all docs/pricing pages never offer an ARM64 sandbox instance type; only one (x86_64-based) sandbox image family is described. Derived absence, not an explicit denial.
